title: [finding] realtime-protocol.mdx teaches a WebSocket rate-limit error shape that no producer emits and no schema declares
body:
Found while fixing #15855 (the `details.retry_after` spelling in the HTTP protocol docs). That card listed `content/docs/protocol/kernel/realtime-protocol.mdx` as a **conditional** fourth site — to be folded in only if the realtime producer also emits `retryAfterSeconds`. It does not, so it is filed here rather than quietly normalised to match a producer it does not have.

Measured on `origin/main` at `9a89a0040`. Every line number below is from that tree.

## What the page teaches

`content/docs/protocol/kernel/realtime-protocol.mdx:1055`, under "Rate Limiting":

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMITED",
    "message": "Too many messages",
    "retry_after": 5,
    "limit": 100,
    "window": "1m"
  }
}
```

## Two things are wrong, and neither is the `details` spelling #15855 fixes

**1. The envelope shape contradicts the only schema that governs realtime error messages.**
`packages/spec/src/api/websocket.zod.ts:362` declares `ErrorMessageSchema` as a **flat** message: `messageId`, `type`, `timestamp` (from `BaseWebSocketMessage` at `:265`), plus `code`, `message`, and an optional `details`. There is no nested `error` object in it. The page wraps every field in one. A client written from this fence reads `msg.error.code` and gets `undefined` against anything the schema governs, because `code` is top-level.

**2. No producer emits it.** Three readings, each with a positive control on the same search so a zero is a reading and not a broken grep:

| reading | result | positive control |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `RATE_LIMITED` in `packages/**` | 5 sites, **none** a realtime emitter — two ADR-0087 connector `targetCode` entries (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:8473`, `packages/spec/src/integration/connector.test.ts:1249`), one automation test, two lines of a plugin-auth email test | `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` in `packages/**` returns 18 hits |
| any WebSocket message rate limiter (`maxMessagesPerMinute`, `messageRateLimit`, `wsRateLimit`) | 0 hits | the phrase `per minute` returns 7 hits in `packages/**` |
| runtime construction of `ErrorMessageSchema` | 0 — the only files naming it are the spec's own `websocket.test.ts` and `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` | the schema itself is exported and parsed by those tests |

The limits the section states in prose (100 messages per minute per connection, 10 subscriptions per minute) are unbacked by the same reading.

## Why this is separate from #15855, not part of it

#15855's fence is "change an occurrence only where it is a **member of a `details` bag**". This `retry_after` is not one: it sits beside `code` and `message` on a nested `error` object the spec does not declare. Correcting only the token would leave the page teaching a shape nothing emits, which is why #15855 carved it out by construction rather than by preference.

## The fix needs a decision first, so this is filed rather than fixed

Two readings lead to opposite edits, and no artefact on this tree settles which:

- **A — the page is wrong.** Rewrite the fence to `ErrorMessageSchema` as declared (flat, with the `details` bag) and drop the unbacked limits.
- **B — the page is a spec for an unshipped capability.** WebSocket message rate limiting is intended, nothing implements it yet, and the page should say so (or the capability should land).

Nothing gates either way: `details` is `z.unknown()`, and these are JSON fences rather than TypeScript, so no check compares a documented realtime envelope against a producer.

Related: #15855.
